purpose: Machine-readable target decisions for the architecture restructuring proposal; not a runtime contract, supported input, or qualification report.
implementation_requires: joint review of upstream contracts, ownership, and migrations
generated current contracts from owning Rust types
retirement: Delete this proposal attachment after its decisions are represented by accepted ADRs, owning types, generated contracts, forward migrations, current documentation, and passing evidence.

scheduler_partition_mapping.tenant_identity_input: The 16 RFC 9562 UUID bytes of the parsed canonical Tenant ResourceId, in network byte order; the nominal text prefix is not input.
scheduler_partition_mapping.partition_id: Unsigned integer represented by the first digest octet
scheduler_partition_mapping.capacity_qualification: Not run; the virtual partition count is a routing choice, not a capacity or availability guarantee.

scheduler_state_ownership.proposed_owner: Scheduling owning types, PostgreSQL scheduling repository, and a new forward migration
scheduler_state_ownership.partition_authority: Partition round, its frozen eligible-tenant keyset upper bound and enumeration cursor only; no tenant deficit JSON
scheduler_state_ownership.tenant_authority: Bounded WDRR deficit, earliest eligible round, credited round, policy version, and Job keyset sweep continuation; not Job readiness or quota
scheduler_state_ownership.row_creation: Provision rows for the closed work-class set in the new Tenant transaction before visibility, taking partition locks in canonical order before tenant/owner locks and assigning participation from the next round; controlled forward backfill provisions existing tenants. Provision a new work class before enabling admission/claim. Ordinary Job creation validates presence and never late-UPSERTs fairness rows
scheduler_state_ownership.row_lifetime: Retain outside candidate windows and across idle periods/restarts until tenant retirement or an explicit audited policy reset
scheduler_state_ownership.growth_bound: One bounded row per actual Tenant and closed work class; no global JSON entry cap that discards accounting
scheduler_state_ownership.migration: Move existing provable accounting out of JSON at a quiesced cutover; remove the old representation, and explicitly audit policy resets where old credits are absent or cannot be translated
scheduler_state_ownership.capacity_qualification: Not run; the table separates authority and bounded access, but is not a measured tenant-count or throughput guarantee.

scheduler_claim_policy.tenant_scan_progress: Freeze the eligible-tenant keyset upper bound for each partition round and persist cursor across transactions; a tenant-window budget only yields, and the next round starts only after the frozen range is complete. New tenants are eligible from the next round even if their UUID sorts inside the current range; no cross-window credit reset or repeated same-round quantum
scheduler_claim_policy.fairness_scope: Exact committed WDRR accounting within a work class and virtual partition, subject to bounded candidate enumeration and eligibility; cross-partition service is approximate.
scheduler_claim_policy.quota_selection: Greedy admissible subset in WDRR proposal order using locked account balances and shadow reservations; a candidate must fit every applicable account.
scheduler_claim_policy.saturated_candidate: Skip without attempt, lease, quota reservation, or successful-service accounting; advance persistent bounded enumeration within the same tenant as well as across tenants.
job_primary_scan_key: nominal Job ResourceId as deterministic tie-breaker
scheduler_claim_policy.job_creation_cutoff: At sweep start freeze a PostgreSQL creation-time cutoff and the immutable keyset upper bound of its visible range; include only Job.created_at strictly before that cutoff. The creation timestamp is sampled by the database when the Job creation statement executes, not inherited from an earlier transaction-start timestamp, supplied/backdated by a client or changed on retry. Later creation cannot enter or extend this sweep
scheduler_claim_policy.job_scan_progress: Persist per-tenant immutable creation-key continuation across transactions; reaching a per-transaction budget only yields without resetting progress. Wrap only after the frozen range is complete. A row created before the cutoff but committed after its key was passed is visited by a subsequent sweep or independent recheck; do not rewind or wait holding Job locks
scheduler_claim_policy.job_scan_eligibility: Current due time, worker compatibility, priority policy and quota are revalidated on each visit, never used as mutable primary cursor keys. Due/priority changes cannot move the same row back into the primary sweep. Enumerate candidates without pre-locking Jobs, then obey parent-owner-to-Job lock order
scheduler_claim_policy.job_head_probe: An independent bounded due/priority/aging probe may accelerate eligible work without changing the primary scan cursor; strict global priority order over all Jobs is not promised
scheduler_claim_policy.deficit_charge: Charge only committed claims; policy quantum accrues once per committed visit round, with the credited round persisted and idle/burst accrual bounded by policy.
scheduler_claim_policy.empty_admissible_batch: Commit scheduler credit/round and enumeration progress atomically, then apply bounded backoff; do not report a dependency outage.
scheduler_claim_policy.work_class_cost_unit: A committed admitted physical attempt; existing continuation rules must not charge an additional attempt merely for a durable wake.
scheduler_claim_policy.partition_mutex: PostgreSQL transaction row lock on scheduler_state; no external scheduler leader lease or durable worker assignment.

authorization_purposes.proposed_owner: Security authorization purpose types and domain command ports
authorization_purposes.new_business_dispatch: Requires current business authorization; revocation prohibits new business effects
authorization_purposes.content_disclosure: Requires current content authorization, including on result and event reads; completion does not grant disclosure
authorization_purposes.restricted_system_completion_reconcile_c: A separately authorized role may record or reconcile an already admitted exact effect, settle quota, cancel, or fulfill exact cleanup despite upstream business revocation; it cannot start new business effects or disclose bodies
authorization_purposes.worker_identity_revocation: The revoked worker cannot commit; an authorized recovery role must take over using a new valid lease and fence

job_execution_requirements.proposed_owner: Typed execution-requirement family in owning Job contracts, domain bindings, WorkerManifest and signed release compatibility closure

families.program: Exact Run definition closure, Program semantic identity and IR ABI
families.validation: Agent compilation/recompilation validation only: exact input identity, compiler semantic identity and compile-policy inputs digest
families.domain_operation: Owning validator/maintenance/control operation ABI and applicable frozen validation-policy, protocol or adapter requirement; includes non-Agent Resource/Artifact validation

job_execution_requirements.run_identity_requirement: Only genuine Run-owned work carries inherited Run execution semantics; other families never create a fake Run or use a zero/sentinel Program identity
job_execution_requirements.validation_scope: Non-Agent validation does not invent an Agent compiler identity; JobKind plus the actual Resource/Artifact owner selects the nominal domain-operation validator requirement, with inapplicable requirements represented by owning typed variants rather than sentinels
job_execution_requirements.routing_consistency: Indexed routing representation is derived from and validated against the nominal payload, JobKind and real owner; it is not independently mutable authority
job_execution_requirements.unsupported_requirement: Durable non-dispatchable compatibility condition; no silent fallback or quota-saturation misclassification
job_execution_requirements.retirement: Check references separately for each family, including pending validation/Draft obligations, public replay/read promises, and non-Run cancellation/reconciliation/cleanup

version_evolution.payload_reader_window_scope: Per owning payload family; retiring a reader is blocked by any live operational or promised public-replay reference that still requires it. Historical archival readers are separately versioned tools, not runtime fallbacks.
version_evolution.semantic_compatibility: Exact admitted semantic identity; a patched build must be explicitly qualified for that identity.
version_evolution.unsupported_existing_run: Remain durable and non-dispatchable with an actionable compatibility condition; never rebind or silently reinterpret.
version_evolution.physical_schema_strategy: One active physical schema and writer generation; controlled writer quiescence for forward schema migration.
version_evolution.semantic_upgrade_of_existing_run: Not supported in place; finish or explicitly terminate the existing Run and create a separately authorized Run with explicit input.
version_evolution.security_patch: Compatible builds can replace a build for an existing semantic identity; incompatible safety fixes require stopping affected new business dispatch and explicit domain disposition while preserving legitimately authorized restricted completion and cleanup.

mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.owner_identity: The exact terminal OAuth Task ResourceId, not its authorization binding, Event, Outbox, or SecretBinding
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.relationship_authority: An optional same-tenant current cleanup Job reference on the shared Task row, outside immutable McpOAuthTaskBinding
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.job_back_reference: Existing immutable Job owner_kind/owner_id; no reverse Job-to-Task foreign key is added
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.effect_identity: The exact terminal Task generation plus its immutable pinned PKCE SecretBinding generation
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.completion_meaning: Exact-generation deletion or independently validated exact-generation absence; never deletion of the current generation by name
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.normal_retry: Reuse the same physical Job and its bounded attempt budget
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.exhausted_recovery: An explicit narrowly authorized idempotent command may replace only a terminal unsuccessful current cleanup Job lacking verified exact deletion; consume a bounded recovery grant and create a new Job plus Task pointer CAS, Receipt and audit evidence in one transaction
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.recovery_preserves: Task generation and resolution, immutable pinned binding, stable logical deletion effect identity, old Job terminal failure and predecessor/recovery authorization history
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.recovery_limits: Owning recovery policy bounds grant validity, recoveries per Task generation and each new physical Job budget; scanners cannot automatically reset or grant budgets
mcp_pkce_cleanup_job.retired_job_fence: Non-current Jobs cannot receive new effect authorization or commit; already admitted in-flight exact deletion is reconciled by the new current Job, never committed through the old Job

outbox_delivery.proposed_owner: platform-contracts committed event delivery boundary types and platform-postgres Outbox repository
outbox_delivery.deployment_owner: Deployment/provisioning contracts own stream lifecycle, subjects, limits, retention, ACL and durable publish ACK semantics across dev, Helm and release
outbox_delivery.publisher_role: Separate Outbox worker package and workload identity with only required Outbox claim/ack, safe Event projection reads and approved subject publish permissions; no business Job or domain mutation authority
outbox_delivery.accepted_confirmation: Successful durable publish ACK for the contracted stream only; disk full, missing stream, ordinary NATS send, timeout or error cannot mark published
outbox_delivery.delivery_semantics: At least once by stable Event identity; consumers must deduplicate or use authority point reads
outbox_delivery.business_work_source: PostgreSQL Jobs; transport loss never removes due work
outbox_delivery.delivery_payload: Closed non-secret committed projection generated from the immutable Event and delivery contract
outbox_delivery.ordering: Per-Run public_sequence or aggregate version remains the logical order; transport is permitted to redeliver or reorder. No total order is promised across aggregates.

public_run_event_retention.proposed_owner: Run persistence owning type and forward migration, public event read/cursor contract and retention command
public_run_event_retention.floor_meaning: Highest public_sequence in the permanently purged continuous prefix
public_run_event_retention.floor_invariant: 0 <= replay_floor <= Run.public_sequence; monotonic across purge and append
public_run_event_retention.purge_atomicity: Acquire the Run exclusive root lock; delete only an eligible continuous prefix and advance replay_floor in the same transaction
public_run_event_retention.cursor_semantics: Cursor records the last accepted public_sequence; a valid cursor below replay_floor returns explicit history unavailable, while equality permits reading the next sequence
public_run_event_retention.read_snapshot: Each initial read and continuation page checks floor, sequence bounds and returned events in one consistent PostgreSQL snapshot
public_run_event_retention.initial_truncation: Without a cursor, a positive floor must be disclosed with the available start boundary; empty retained history must not imply an untruncated Run

joint_restore_writer_isolation.proposed_owner: Deployment recovery contract and existing domain recovery commands
joint_restore_writer_isolation.isolation: Stop old writers, revoke old workload/provider/control identities, terminate old database sessions and rotate affected credentials before restoring writes
joint_restore_writer_isolation.resumption: Use new process generations and legitimate recovery roles; retain domain effect identities and fence checks, reconcile uncertain external effects before new dispatch
